source_basis: The Summary opens with two requested outputs, announces two foundational models, then gives one application paragraph for leaf shape and one for leaf mass.
interpretation: A reusable A-summary can move from target to model architecture and then repeat task-method-result-boundary blocks for each application; this supports LP-A-ABS-PARAGRAPH-CHAIN when the final interpretation is explicitly bounded.
counterevidence: The second application reports no error metric and neither branch gives a decision consequence.

source_basis: The Summary gives the vector-tree model and sunlight model separate bullets, each naming its representation, physical output, and core assumption or governing equation.
interpretation: Model bullets are reusable when they state role and handoff, but complementary geometry and irradiance models must not be rewritten as a baseline-to-extension staircase.

source_basis: The leaf-shape paragraph holds branching structure fixed, tests three shapes on weighted sunlight exposure, compares the selected shape with the observed species shape, and reports a size-dependent failure regime.
interpretation: This independently supports task-method-result and boundary language: name the held-fixed structure, candidate count, common metric, comparator, result, and failure regime.
counterevidence: Three candidates cannot establish a global maximum and no match tolerance is defined.

source_basis: The Summary states that the algorithm works for medium and small leaves but becomes unreliable and high-variance for large leaves.
interpretation: A front-page boundary is valuable when it identifies the supported regime, failure regime, and symptom; good, unreliable, and large variance should be replaced by measured thresholds.

source_basis: The second Summary application names the tree profile, photosynthesis model, LMA, LAI, one species case, and a limited-data comparison.
interpretation: Task-method-result language should expose the exact indices and final identity rather than say indexes like, and external comparison must name the observed value, error, and acceptance threshold.
counterevidence: The Summary says accurate enough but reports no observed leaf mass or metric.

source_basis: The Outline explicitly lists two models followed by two applications in body order and names the output of each model.
interpretation: This is a strong fifth independent example of LP-A-INT-METHOD-ROADMAP: an introduction should preview the actual dependency order rather than list section titles alone.

source_basis: The paragraph uses Given, Then, Thus, and Finally to trace tree profile to per-leaf irradiance, per-leaf LMA, weighted LMA, crown area, and total leaf mass.
interpretation: Sequential transitions are reusable only when every sentence consumes a named output from the preceding stage; the chain should end with the unit-bearing final identity.
counterevidence: The later body never defines the LMA weighting rule.

source_basis: The introduction says the same tree profile is retained while leaf shape changes, then uses one exposure metric to select a shape.
interpretation: Holding fixed is a useful comparison frame, but the prose must list every controlled quantity and avoid causal interpretation from an uncalibrated shape match.
counterevidence: Leaf size, placement, and candidate-space coverage are not fully controlled.

source_basis: The Summary uses real-life data, generally maximize, good for, and accurate enough without dataset provenance or performance thresholds.
interpretation: These phrases should be replaced by the case count, candidate count, named dataset, metric, value, uncertainty, and supported scope.
counterevidence: The Summary does at least disclose limited data and the large-leaf failure regime.

section: 8 Letter to a scientific journal editor
source_basis: The letter reorganizes findings into two audience-facing claims and two model contributions, but uses proven viable, always adopts, stunning power, solid evidence, and innovative.
interpretation: Stakeholder prose may foreground findings and named metrics, but it must retain candidate-space, validation, and causal boundaries rather than strengthen them for rhetorical effect.

source_basis: The outline names profile, irradiance, photosynthesis, per-leaf LMA, weighted LMA, projected crown area, LAI, and total mass in execution order.
interpretation: A multistage roadmap is useful only if each body section later defines the handoff variable, units, aggregation, calibration, and validation.
counterevidence: Several body handoffs remain verbal or uncalibrated.

source_basis: Leaf spacing d(I) and budding probability p(I) require irradiance, while crown irradiance requires the leaf placement and crown geometry that those functions generate.
interpretation: The dependency graph contains an unresolved feedback loop; the paper needs an initialization and fixed-point, sequential, or iterative coupling procedure.

source_basis: The vector-tree model supplies geometry while the sunlight model supplies a directional physical field; both feed two later applications.
interpretation: These models form complementary typed interfaces, not a baseline followed by a fuller extension. Pattern mining must preserve dependency type instead of treating all ordered prose as a staircase.

source_basis: The paper says the hypothesis stands and proves insight, then immediately says a larger pool is required before a solid conclusion.
interpretation: The conclusion must be reordered as tested result, evidence boundary, then bounded interpretation; a later caveat does not repair an earlier proof claim.

source_basis: A local rotation-scaling matrix recursively maps parent vectors to child vectors and accumulates global endpoints.
interpretation: Recursive geometry should record coordinate frames, transform order, length scaling, termination, parameter distributions, and collision constraints before the resulting crown is used physically.

source_basis: The paper identifies terminal branches and four phyllotaxis families but leaves the irradiance-to-spacing d(I) and irradiance-to-budding p(I) functions unspecified.
interpretation: Naming a biological mechanism is not a closed placement model; both functions need domains, ranges, calibration data, sampling rules, and physical bounds.

source_basis: The model combines annual sky brightness, exponential Monsi-Saeki attenuation, crown path length, and a directional hemisphere integral.
interpretation: The geometry-field handoff is reusable when the sky boundary, directional measure, extinction units, ray path, quadrature, and field validation are all explicit.
counterevidence: The printed angular weight and phi definition are internally inconsistent.

source_basis: Directional projected shadow scores are integrated against sky brightness and normalized before four leaf shapes are ranked.
interpretation: A finite held-structure shape comparison needs a union-area definition, positive normalized weights, grid convergence, uncertainty, and candidate-space bounds before argmax interpretation.

source_basis: Gross photosynthesis, respiration, and CO2 diffusion are combined into a quadratic for net photosynthesis and a printed root expression.
interpretation: A physiological algebraic handoff must define parameter values, admissible roots, units, and substitution checks; the printed root cannot be used because it does not solve the preceding quadratic.

source_basis: The synthesis links net photosynthesis to venation-based LMA, averages individual LMA values, projects crown area, multiplies by LAI, and ends with mass equals weighted LMA times total leaf area.
interpretation: The final identity is interpretable, but every local-to-crown handoff requires a weight, unit, individual-tree measurement, uncertainty, and observed mass target.

source_basis: Thirty-two possible coordinate systems are created from measured outgoing rays, and the authors visually choose the simulated profile closest to the real tree.
interpretation: This is manual profile selection, not quantitative calibration; it needs measured branch coordinates, a prespecified loss, uncertainty, and held-out validation.

source_basis: The case study assumes d(I) follows N(0.1,0.1) without stating whether the second value is variance or standard deviation or how irradiance enters.
interpretation: A distributional assumption must match the modeled function, respect physical support, state parameter meaning, and be estimated or sensitivity-tested.

source_basis: The printed integral uses cos(theta)sin(phi) while phi is defined as azimuth over 0 to 2pi, and no measured irradiance comparison is supplied.
interpretation: Directional integrals require a coordinate/Jacobian audit, dimensional check, positive-weight test, numerical convergence, and field measurements before physical use.

source_basis: Three tree profiles are each evaluated on four shapes and the selected category matches the depicted real leaf class; no holdout, match metric, or uncertainty is reported.
interpretation: This is a three-case worked comparison, not validation of a general leaf-shape law; rankings need resampling, perturbation, candidate expansion, and independent species cases.
counterevidence: The paper itself calls for a larger pool of tree profiles.

source_basis: The displayed P_n root has a leading negative bracket and a discriminant that omits the constant term required by the preceding quadratic.
interpretation: Equation-to-derivation parity and root substitution must pass before a formula feeds downstream LMA; biological validity cannot repair an algebraically inconsistent root.

source_basis: For the triangular, elliptic, and semi-spherical profiles, the largest reported score corresponds to the displayed pine, poplar, and Japanese banana leaf classes.
interpretation: The table establishes the finite-candidate outputs for three cases; it does not establish global optimality, causality, or robust separation, especially where 0.83 and 0.85 are close.

source_basis: The case study reports ground area 6.001436 m^2, LAI 12, LMA 177.74 g/m^2, and total leaf mass 12777.84 g, but the multiplication line uses 177.47 g/m^2.
interpretation: The output is reproducible accounting only after resolving the LMA mismatch; without an observed leaf mass it remains a prediction rather than empirical validation.

source_basis: Regression on 30 simulated cases shows weak pooled association and stronger within-profile trends, after which the paper says a cubic relation appears but limited data require further testing.
interpretation: The result is exploratory evidence that profile stratification matters; it does not validate a universal cubic mass-height law.
counterevidence: All 30 cases are simulated rather than observed trees.

source_basis: Three-dimensional crown figures show overhead and oblique sun directions with projected pink shadow points below the tree.
interpretation: Mechanism-aligned views make a directional projection model inspectable, but the figure should identify leaf polygons, union shadow, scale, viewing direction, and the exact area used in SE.

source_basis: Four small scatter plots show pooled and profile-specific simulated mass-height relationships without fitted equations, uncertainty, residuals, or readable axis detail.
interpretation: A scaling-law visual should align raw points, fitted curve, sample size, uncertainty, residuals, and simulation-versus-observation status before supporting a functional claim.

source_basis: The case study measures trunk and outgoing-ray directions, chooses 32 coordinate systems, borrows leaf dimensions from a manual, and selects LAI=12 from literature rather than measuring the target tree.
interpretation: A field-to-model record must distinguish measured, visually selected, literature-transferred, and assumed inputs, with uncertainty for every category.

source_basis: The supplied usefulArea routine rotates branch-point coordinates and counts occupied grid cells; it does not project explicit leaf polygons even though the body defines SE from individual leaf shadows.
interpretation: The code and equation implement different geometric objects, so the reported exposure score needs an equation-code-object parity audit before reuse.
counterevidence: Publishing the code makes the mismatch discoverable.
